BD-01.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Almost every BCS and bank exam has one question on the oldest janapada, Mahasthangarh, Shashanka or matsyanyaya. Janapada → present-day area matching is the most common pattern.

## The name "Bangla / Bengal"
- The word **"বঙ্গ" (Vanga)** is first mentioned in the **ঐতরেয় আরণ্যক (Aitareya Aranyaka)**.
- **আবুল ফজল**, in **আইন-ই-আকবরী**, explained "Bangal" as **বঙ্গ + আল** (আল = embankment/dyke).
- 🔥 Sultan **শামসুদ্দিন ইলিয়াস শাহ** united the whole region in the 14th century and took the title **"শাহ-ই-বাঙ্গালাহ"**. From then on, the whole region was called **"বাঙ্গালাহ"**.

## Ancient janapadas (প্রাচীন জনপদ) 🔥
In ancient times Bengal was not one country. It was divided into many small regions called **জনপদ**.

| Janapada | Present-day area | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| **পুণ্ড্র (Pundra)** | Bogura, Rajshahi, Dinajpur (North Bengal) | 🔥 **Oldest janapada.** Capital **পুণ্ড্রনগর = মহাস্থানগড়** (Bogura) |
| **বরেন্দ্র (Varendra)** | Bogura, Rajshahi, Dinajpur | Part of Pundra; between the Ganga and the Karatoya |
| **বঙ্গ (Vanga)** | Dhaka, Faridpur, Bikrampur area | The name "Bangladesh" comes from this |
| **গৌড় (Gauda)** | Murshidabad, Malda, Chapainawabganj | **Shashanka's** kingdom |
| **সমতট (Samatata)** | **Cumilla & Noakhali** | Mentioned in Samudragupta's Allahabad inscription |
| **হরিকেল (Harikela)** | Eastern Bengal (Sylhet – Chattogram) | |
| **চন্দ্রদ্বীপ (Chandradwip)** | **Barishal** | Old name of Barishal |
| **রাঢ় (Radha)** | West of the Bhagirathi (West Bengal) | |
| **তাম্রলিপ্ত (Tamralipta)** | Midnapore (West Bengal) | Famous ancient **seaport** |
| **শ্রীহট্ট (Srihatta)** | Sylhet | |

**Memory tip:** পুণ্ড্র = বগুড়া (মহাস্থান); সমতট = কুমিল্লা-নোয়াখালী; চন্দ্রদ্বীপ = বরিশাল; হরিকেল = সিলেট-চট্টগ্রাম.

## Important archaeological sites
- 🔥 **মহাস্থানগড় (Bogura):** on the bank of the **করতোয়া** river. It is the **oldest city-site** in Bangladesh. The **Mahasthan Brahmi inscription** (Maurya period) found here is the **oldest inscription found in Bangladesh**.
- **উয়ারী-বটেশ্বর (Narsingdi):** a fort-city about **2,500 years old**. **Jahangirnagar University** has excavated it since **2000**. It shows ancient trade links.

## Gangaridai and Alexander
- **Alexander the Great** invaded India in **326 BCE**.
- Greek writers mention a powerful kingdom called **গঙ্গারিডই (Gangaridai)** in the Ganges delta. Its strength was one reason Alexander did not advance further east.

## Maurya Empire (মৌর্য সাম্রাজ্য)
- Founder: **চন্দ্রগুপ্ত মৌর্য** (c. 321 BCE). Capital: **পাটলিপুত্র**.
- His adviser **কৌটিল্য (চাণক্য)** wrote **"অর্থশাস্ত্র"**.
- Greek ambassador **মেগাস্থিনিস** wrote **"ইন্ডিকা"**.
- **সম্রাট অশোক** accepted **Buddhism** after the **Kalinga War (261 BCE)**.
- North Bengal (Pundra) was part of the Maurya Empire. **The Mahasthan Brahmi inscription is the proof.**

## Gupta Empire (গুপ্ত সাম্রাজ্য)
- Founder: **শ্রীগুপ্ত**. **প্রথম চন্দ্রগুপ্ত** started the Gupta era in **320 CE**.
- 🔥 **সমুদ্রগুপ্ত** is called the **"Napoleon of India"**. His **Allahabad pillar inscription** (written by **Harisena**) names **সমতট** as a frontier (প্রত্যন্ত) kingdom.
- **দ্বিতীয় চন্দ্রগুপ্ত (বিক্রমাদিত্য):** Chinese traveller **ফা-হিয়েন** visited India in his reign.
- The Gupta period is called the **"Golden Age"** of ancient India.

## Shashanka (শশাঙ্ক) 🔥
- The **first independent, sovereign king of Bengal (বাংলার প্রথম স্বাধীন সার্বভৌম রাজা)**, early 7th century.
- Kingdom: **গৌড়**. Capital: **কর্ণসুবর্ণ** (Murshidabad, West Bengal).
- His main rival was **হর্ষবর্ধন** of Thaneswar/Kanauj.
- Chinese traveller **হিউয়েন সাং** visited Bengal in the 7th century.
- He died around **637 CE** (some sources say 638).
- Note: some writers credit Shashanka with starting the Bengali calendar (বঙ্গাব্দ), but the common exam answer for the introducer of the Bangla san is **Emperor Akbar**.

## Matsyanyaya (মাৎস্যন্যায়) 🔥
- After Shashanka's death, Bengal fell into anarchy for about **100 years (mid-7th to mid-8th century)**.
- **মাৎস্যন্যায়** means "the rule of fish": big fish eat small fish, the strong oppress the weak.
- It ended when the leaders chose **গোপাল** as king (c. **750 CE**). Gopala founded the **পাল বংশ** (see BD-02).

**Memory hook:** *পুণ্ড্র প্রাচীন → মৌর্য → গুপ্ত → শশাঙ্ক (প্রথম স্বাধীন) → মাৎস্যন্যায় → গোপাল (পাল)*

## Timeline
| Year | Event | Key person |
|---|---|---|
| 326 BCE | Alexander's invasion; Gangaridai mentioned | Alexander |
| c. 321 BCE | Maurya Empire founded | Chandragupta Maurya |
| 261 BCE | Kalinga War; Ashoka turns to Buddhism | Ashoka |
| 320 CE | Gupta era begins | Chandragupta I |
| early 7th c. | First independent kingdom of Bengal (Gauda) | Shashanka |
| c. 650–750 | Matsyanyaya (anarchy) | — |
| c. 750 | Pala dynasty founded by election | Gopala |

## Quick revision
- Oldest janapada: **পুণ্ড্র**; capital **পুণ্ড্রনগর (মহাস্থানগড়, বগুড়া)**.
- Mahasthangarh stands on the **করতোয়া** river; oldest city-site of Bangladesh.
- Oldest inscription in Bangladesh: **Mahasthan Brahmi inscription** (Maurya).
- Samatata = **Cumilla–Noakhali**; Chandradwip = **Barishal**; Harikela = **Sylhet–Chattogram**.
- Wari-Bateshwar is in **Narsingdi**, about 2,500 years old.
- Samudragupta = **"Napoleon of India"**; Allahabad inscription written by **Harisena**.
- Fa-Hien came in the time of **Chandragupta II**; Hiuen Tsang in the **7th century**.
- First independent king of Bengal: **শশাঙ্ক**; capital **কর্ণসুবর্ণ**.
- Matsyanyaya lasted about **100 years**; ended with **Gopala** (c. 750).

BD-02.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask who founded the Palas, who built Paharpur, the longest-ruling dynasty, Atish Dipankar, the Kaivarta revolt, Ballal Sena's kulinism and Lakshman Sena's fall to Bakhtiyar Khalji.

## Pala dynasty (পাল বংশ, c. 750 – 12th century) 🔥
- Founded by **গোপাল**, who was **elected (নির্বাচিত)** by the local chiefs around **750 CE** to end **মাৎস্যন্যায়**. This is often cited as the first example of an elected king in Bengal.
- The Palas ruled for about **400 years**: the **longest-ruling dynasty** in the history of Bengal.
- Religion: **Buddhism (বৌদ্ধ)**. They patronised Buddhist monasteries and learning.
- The oldest specimen of Bangla literature, the **চর্যাপদ**, was composed in the Pala period.

| King | Key facts |
|---|---|
| **গোপাল** | Founder; elected king (c. 750) |
| 🔥 **ধর্মপাল** (c. 781–821) | Greatest Pala king in power; built **সোমপুর মহাবিহার (Paharpur, Naogaon)** and **বিক্রমশীলা মহাবিহার** (Bihar); fought the **ত্রিপক্ষীয় সংগ্রাম** for Kanauj |
| **দেবপাল** | Empire at its widest; patron of **Nalanda** |
| **প্রথম মহীপাল** | Revived the empire; called the **"second founder" of the Pala dynasty** |
| **দ্বিতীয় মহীপাল** | Faced the **Kaivarta revolt (কৈবর্ত বিদ্রোহ)**; killed by rebels |
| **রামপাল** | Recovered Varendra from the Kaivartas; his life is told in **সন্ধ্যাকর নন্দীর "রামচরিত"** |
| **মদনপাল** | Commonly named as the last notable Pala king |

### Tripartite struggle (ত্রিপক্ষীয় সংগ্রাম)
A long three-way war for control of **Kanauj** among the **Palas (Bengal)**, the **Gurjara-Pratiharas** and the **Rashtrakutas**.

### Kaivarta revolt (কৈবর্ত বিদ্রোহ) 🔥
- Led by **দিব্য (দিব্যোক)**, a Kaivarta chief, against Mahipala II. The rebels captured **Varendra**.
- It is often called the **first successful rebellion / peasant revolt** in Bengal's history.
- **দিব্যক জয়স্তম্ভ** (Dibar Dighi, Naogaon) is linked to it.

### Somapura Mahavihara (Paharpur) 🔥
- In **Naogaon** district; built by **Dharmapala**.
- One of the largest Buddhist monasteries south of the Himalayas.
- **UNESCO World Heritage Site (1985)**.

## Atish Dipankar (অতীশ দীপঙ্কর) 🔥
- Born **982 CE** at **বজ্রযোগিনী, বিক্রমপুর (Munshiganj)**.
- Great Buddhist scholar; head (অধ্যক্ষ) of **Vikramashila** monastery.
- Went to **Tibet** (1042) on invitation and died there (1053).

## Other dynasties of the period (south-east Bengal)
| Dynasty | Key fact |
|---|---|
| **দেব বংশ** | **শালবন বিহার (Mainamati, Cumilla)** was built by **শ্রীভবদেব** of this dynasty |
| **চন্দ্র বংশ** | Ruled Vanga-Samatata in the 10th–11th century; best-known king **শ্রীচন্দ্র**; capital **বিক্রমপুর** |
| **বর্মন বংশ** | Ruled East Bengal after the Chandras; capital Vikrampur |

## Sena dynasty (সেন বংশ) 🔥
- The Senas came from **কর্ণাট (Karnataka, South India)**. They were **Hindu (Brahmanical)** and patrons of **Sanskrit**.
- Founder: **সামন্ত সেন**. The first independent Sena king who built the kingdom was **বিজয় সেন** (he defeated the last Palas).
- Capitals: **বিজয়পুর**, later **বিক্রমপুর**; Lakshman Sena lived at **নদীয়া (নুদিয়া)**.

| King | Key facts |
|---|---|
| **সামন্ত সেন** | Founder of the line |
| **বিজয় সেন** | Real founder of Sena rule in Bengal |
| 🔥 **বল্লাল সেন** | Introduced **কৌলীন্য প্রথা (kulinism)**; wrote **"দানসাগর"** and started **"অদ্ভুতসাগর"** |
| 🔥 **লক্ষ্মণ সেন** | Last powerful Sena king; completed "অদ্ভুতসাগর"; fled when **বখতিয়ার খলজি** attacked Nadia (1204) |

### Lakshman Sena's court poets (পঞ্চরত্ন)
- **জয়দেব** — **"গীতগোবিন্দ"**
- **ধোয়ী** — **"পবনদূত"**
- **হলায়ুধ** — **"ব্রাহ্মণসর্বস্ব"**
- Also **উমাপতি ধর** and **শরণ**.

### End of the Senas
- In **1204** (some sources: 1203 or 1205) **ইখতিয়ার উদ্দিন মুহম্মদ বিন বখতিয়ার খলজি** attacked **Nadia** with about **17–18 horsemen**; Lakshman Sena fled to **Vikrampur**. This began Muslim rule in Bengal (see BD-03).
- Sena rule continued in East Bengal (Vikrampur) for some decades under his sons.

## Pala vs Sena
| | Pala | Sena |
|---|---|---|
| Religion | Buddhist | Hindu (Brahmanical) |
| Origin | Local (Bengal) | Karnataka (South India) |
| Duration | ~400 years | ~100+ years |
| Famous for | Paharpur, Vikramashila, Charyapada | Kulinism, Sanskrit literature |

## Quick revision
- Pala founder **Gopala**, elected c. **750**; dynasty ruled ~**400 years** (longest).
- **Dharmapala** built **Paharpur (Somapura) Vihara** and **Vikramashila**.
- **Mahipala I** = second founder of the Palas.
- **Kaivarta revolt** leader **Divya (Divyok)**; Ramacharita by **Sandhyakar Nandi**.
- **Atish Dipankar**: born 982, Bajrayogini, Munshiganj; died in Tibet.
- **Shalban Vihara** (Mainamati) built by **Bhavadeva** of the Deva dynasty.
- Senas came from **Karnataka**; **Ballal Sena** introduced **kulinism**.
- **Jayadeva** wrote **Gitagovinda** in Lakshman Sena's court.
- **Bakhtiyar Khalji** took Nadia in **1204**.

BD-03.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Standard questions: year of Muslim conquest (1204), first independent sultan (Fakhruddin Mubarak Shah), "Shah-i-Bangalah" (Iliyas Shah), golden age (Hussain Shah), Adina and Sixty Dome mosques, and Ibn Battuta.

## Bakhtiyar Khalji and the Muslim conquest 🔥
- **ইখতিয়ার উদ্দিন মুহম্মদ বিন বখতিয়ার খলজি**, a Turkish general, attacked **Nadia** in **1204** (some sources: 1203 or 1205) with about **17–18 horsemen**. **Lakshman Sena** fled.
- He made **লখনৌতি (Lakhnauti / Gaur)** his capital. This began **Muslim rule in Bengal**.
- He built mosques, madrasas and khanqahs.
- His **Tibet campaign failed**; on return he died at **দেবকোট** in **1206** (he was killed by **Ali Mardan Khalji**).
- The main source: **মিনহাজ-উস-সিরাজ**, **"তবকাত-ই-নাসিরী"**.

## After Bakhtiyar (1206–1338)
- **গিয়াসউদ্দিন ইওয়াজ খলজি** strengthened Lakhnauti and built a navy.
- Bengal often rebelled against Delhi, so historian **জিয়াউদ্দিন বারানী** called it **"বুলগাকপুর" (land of rebels)**.
- Delhi governors ruled from three centres: **Lakhnauti, Satgaon, Sonargaon**.

## Independent Sultanate (স্বাধীন সুলতানি যুগ, 1338–1538) 🔥
- **ফখরুদ্দিন মুবারক শাহ** declared independence at **সোনারগাঁও** in **1338**: the **first independent sultan** of (east) Bengal.
- 🔥 The Moroccan traveller **ইবনে বতুতা** visited Bengal in **1346** in his reign. He called Bengal **"দোজখপুর নিয়ামত"** (a hell full of good things). His travel book is **"কিতাবুল রেহলা"**.
- The independent sultanate lasted about **200 years (1338–1538)**.

## Iliyas Shahi dynasty (ইলিয়াস শাহী বংশ) 🔥
| Ruler | Key facts |
|---|---|
| 🔥 **শামসুদ্দিন ইলিয়াস শাহ** | United Lakhnauti, Satgaon and Sonargaon (by **1352**). Title **"শাহ-ই-বাঙ্গালাহ"**; the whole region came to be called **বাঙ্গালাহ**. Capital **পাণ্ডুয়া**. Resisted Delhi Sultan **ফিরোজ শাহ তুঘলক** (siege of **একডালা দুর্গ**) |
| **সিকান্দার শাহ** | Built the **আদিনা মসজিদ** at Pandua (1370s), the largest mosque of its time in the subcontinent |
| 🔥 **গিয়াসউদ্দিন আযম শাহ** | Famous for justice (story of the **Qazi's judgment**). Exchanged letters with Persian poet **হাফিজ**. Poet **শাহ মুহম্মদ সগীর** wrote **"ইউসুফ-জোলেখা"** in his time |

- **রাজা গণেশ** briefly seized power; his son **যদু** became Muslim as **জালালউদ্দিন মুহম্মদ শাহ**.
- The Iliyas Shahi line was **restored** under **নাসিরউদ্দিন মাহমুদ শাহ**. In his time **খান জাহান আলী** built the 🔥 **ষাট গম্বুজ মসজিদ (Sixty Dome Mosque), Bagerhat** — a **UNESCO World Heritage Site (1985)**.
- **রুকনুদ্দিন বারবক শাহ** brought in **Habshi (Abyssinian)** guards. Poet **মালাধর বসু** ("শ্রীকৃষ্ণবিজয়") got the title **"গুণরাজ খান"** from him.

## Habshi rule (1487–1493)
- Abyssinian (Habshi) slave-officers seized the throne and ruled for about **6 years** — a period of disorder.

## Hussain Shahi dynasty (হোসেন শাহী বংশ, 1493–1538) 🔥
| Ruler | Key facts |
|---|---|
| 🔥 **আলাউদ্দিন হোসেন শাহ** (1493–1519) | Best sultan; his rule is called the **golden age** of the sultanate. Hindu poets praised him as **"নৃপতি তিলক"**, **"জগৎভূষণ"**, **"কৃষ্ণাবতার"**. **শ্রীচৈতন্য** lived in his time. **ছোট সোনা মসজিদ** (Shibganj, Chapainawabganj) was built in his reign |
| **নাসিরউদ্দিন নুসরত শাহ** | Built **বড় সোনা মসজিদ** and **কদম রসুল** at Gaur |
| **গিয়াসউদ্দিন মাহমুদ শাহ** | Last Hussain Shahi sultan; defeated by **শেরশাহ** in **1538** |

- Bangla literature flourished: Hussain Shah's generals **পরাগল খান** and **ছুটি খান** (Chattogram) sponsored Bangla **Mahabharata** translations (**কবীন্দ্র পরমেশ্বর**, **শ্রীকর নন্দী**). **বিজয়গুপ্ত** wrote **"মনসামঙ্গল"**.

## Sher Shah and the Karranis
- **শেরশাহ** defeated Humayun at **Chausa (1539)** and **Kanauj (1540)**.
- He built the **Grand Trunk Road ("সড়ক-ই-আজম")** from **Sonargaon to Peshawar**, introduced the **"রুপি"** coin, and started horse-post (ডাক) service.
- The **কররানী** dynasty followed. **দাউদ খান কররানী**, the **last independent sultan of Bengal**, was defeated and killed by the Mughals at the **Battle of Rajmahal (1576)**.

BD-04.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask when Dhaka became capital (1610), who led the Baro Bhuiyans (Isa Khan), Shaista Khan's cheap rice and Lalbagh Fort, and who moved the capital to Murshidabad (Murshid Quli Khan).

## The Mughals reach Bengal
- **বাবর** founded the Mughal Empire after the **First Battle of Panipat (1526)**.
- **আকবর**'s army defeated **Daud Khan Karrani** at the **Battle of Rajmahal (1576)**. But local chiefs kept resisting, so full Mughal control came only under **জাহাঙ্গীর**.
- Akbar is credited with starting the **Bengali calendar (বঙ্গাব্দ)**, based on his **ফসলি সন**, with the help of **আমির ফতেহউল্লাহ সিরাজী**.

## Baro Bhuiyans (বারো ভূঁইয়া) 🔥
- Powerful landlords/chiefs of Bengal who resisted Mughal rule in the late 16th – early 17th century. "Baro" (twelve) means "many"; the number was not exactly twelve.
- 🔥 Leader: **ঈসা খাঁ**. Capital: **সোনারগাঁও**; he had a stronghold at **কাত্রাবো**. He fought **Man Singh**, Akbar's general, and took the title **"মসনদ-ই-আলা"**.
- After Isa Khan's death (1599), his son **মুসা খাঁ** led the resistance. He was finally defeated by Subedar **ইসলাম খাঁ** (1611).

| **প্রতাপাদিত্য** | Jashore (Jessore) |
| **ফজল গাজী** | Bhawal (Gazipur) |

## Dhaka becomes the capital 🔥
- Subedar **ইসলাম খাঁ** moved the capital of **Suba Bangla** from **রাজমহল** to **ঢাকা** in **1610** (some sources: 1608).
- He named Dhaka **"জাহাঙ্গীরনগর"** after Emperor Jahangir.

### Lalbagh Fort (লালবাগ কেল্লা) 🔥
- Started in **1678** by Prince **মুহম্মদ আজম** (son of Aurangzeb). Its old name was **আওরঙ্গবাদ কেল্লা**.
- **Shaista Khan** continued it but left it **incomplete** after the death of his daughter **পরী বিবি**, whose tomb is inside the fort.

## Nawabi period (নবাবী আমল)
- 🔥 **মুর্শিদকুলী খান**: first Nawab of Bengal (practically independent while accepting the Mughal emperor). He moved the capital from **Dhaka to Murshidabad (মকসুদাবাদ)** in **1717** (the Diwani office moved earlier, around 1704). He introduced the **"মাল জামিনী"** revenue system.
- **সুজাউদ্দিন খান** and **সরফরাজ খান** followed.
- **আলীবর্দী খান** (1740–1756): seized power by defeating Sarfaraz Khan at the **Battle of Giria (1740)**. Bengal suffered **Maratha raids (বর্গির হাঙ্গামা)** in his time; the Maratha commander was **ভাস্কর পণ্ডিত**.
- **সিরাজউদ্দৌলা** (1756–1757): grandson of Alivardi; the **last independent Nawab of Bengal** (see BD-05).

BD-05.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Plassey (23 June 1757) is one of the most-asked dates in all exams. Also asked: the conspirators, Buxar (1764), the Dewani grant (1765), dual government and the famine of 1770 (ছিয়াত্তরের মন্বন্তর).

## Siraj-ud-Daulah (সিরাজউদ্দৌলা)
- Grandson of **Alivardi Khan**; became Nawab in **April 1756** at a young age (about 23).
- Enemies inside the family: his aunt **ঘসেটি বেগম** and cousin **শওকত জং** (Nawab of Purnia).
- Conflict with the English: they fortified **Calcutta (Fort William)** without permission, misused trade permits (দস্তক) and sheltered **কৃষ্ণদাস**, a fugitive.
- Siraj captured the **Kasimbazar** factory and **Calcutta (June 1756)** and renamed Calcutta **"আলীনগর"**.
- **অন্ধকূপ হত্যা (Black Hole tragedy):** a story of English prisoners dying in a small room, told by **হলওয়েল**. Historians consider it **greatly exaggerated or invented**.
- **Clive** and **Admiral Watson** retook Calcutta (January 1757); Siraj had to sign the **Treaty of Alinagar (February 1757)**.

## Battle of Plassey (পলাশীর যুদ্ধ) 🔥🔥
- **Date: 23 June 1757.** Place: **পলাশীর আম্রকানন**, on the bank of the **ভাগীরথী** (Nadia district, West Bengal).
- English commander: **রবার্ট ক্লাইভ**.
- Result: the Nawab's army lost because of **betrayal**, not strength. This began British rule in Bengal (and later India).

| Side | People |
|---|---|
| 🔥 **Conspirators (traitors)** | **মীর জাফর** (commander-in-chief/প্রধান সেনাপতি), **জগৎ শেঠ**, **রায় দুর্লভ**, **উমিচাঁদ (আমির চাঁদ)**, **ইয়ার লতিফ**, **ঘসেটি বেগম** |
| **Loyal to Siraj** | **মীর মদন** (killed in battle), **মোহনলাল**, French officer **সিনফ্রে** |

- Siraj fled but was captured and **killed on 2 July 1757** by **মোহাম্মদী বেগ** on the orders of Mir Jafar's son **মীরন**.

## After Plassey: puppet Nawabs
| Nawab | Period | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| **মীর জাফর** | 1757–1760 | Puppet of the English; gave huge sums of money and land to the Company |
| 🔥 **মীর কাসিম** | 1760–1763 | Able ruler; moved capital to **মুঙ্গের (Munger)**; abolished internal duty for everyone, which angered the English; fought them |
| **মীর জাফর** (again) | 1763–1765 | Restored by the English |
| **নাজমুদ্দৌলা** | 1765 onward | Nawab only in name |

- **Robert Clive** became the **first Governor of Bengal (1758)**.

## Battle of Buxar (বক্সারের যুদ্ধ) 🔥
- **Date: 22 October 1764.** Place: Buxar, Bihar.
- **Allies (against the English):** **মীর কাসিম** + **সুজাউদ্দৌলা** (Nawab of Awadh/অযোধ্যা) + Mughal emperor **দ্বিতীয় শাহ আলম**.
- English commander: **হেক্টর মনরো**. The English won.
- Plassey was won by treachery; **Buxar was a real military victory**, and it made the English the true power of north-east India.

## The Dewani (দেওয়ানি লাভ) 🔥
- **Treaty of Allahabad, 12 August 1765:** Emperor **Shah Alam II** granted the **Dewani (right to collect revenue)** of **বাংলা, বিহার ও উড়িষ্যা** to the East India Company.
- In return the Company paid the emperor **26 lakh rupees a year**.

## Dual government (দ্বৈত শাসন)
- Introduced by **Clive** in **1765**: the Company held the **Dewani (revenue)**, while the Nawab kept the **Nizamat (administration, law and order)** but had no money or power. Power without responsibility for the Company; responsibility without power for the Nawab.
- 🔥 Result: the **ছিয়াত্তরের মন্বন্তর** — the great famine of **1770** (Bangla year **১১৭৬**). About **one-third** of Bengal's people died.
- **Warren Hastings** abolished dual government in **1772**.
- Under the **Regulating Act 1773**, Warren Hastings became the **first Governor-General (of Bengal)** in **1774**.

BD-06.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Common questions: who introduced the Permanent Settlement and when (Cornwallis, 1793), Titumir's bamboo fort, founder of the Faraizi movement, "Nil Darpan", and where the 1857 revolt began.

## Land revenue systems 🔥
| Year | System | Introduced by |
|---|---|---|
| 1772 | **পাঁচসালা বন্দোবস্ত** (five-year settlement) | **Warren Hastings** |
| 1777 | **একসালা বন্দোবস্ত** (one-year settlement) | Warren Hastings |
| 1790 | **দশসালা বন্দোবস্ত** (ten-year settlement) | **Lord Cornwallis** |
| **22 March 1793** | 🔥 **চিরস্থায়ী বন্দোবস্ত (Permanent Settlement)** | **Lord Cornwallis** |

### Permanent Settlement — key points
- Zamindars became the **permanent owners** of land; the revenue they paid to the Government was **fixed forever**.
- **সূর্যাস্ত আইন (Sunset Law):** if a zamindar failed to pay revenue by sunset on the fixed day, his estate was auctioned.
- Effects: a new loyal **zamindar class** grew; peasants (রায়ত) were exploited; many old zamindar families lost their land; absentee landlordism and sub-infeudation (পত্তনি) spread.
- It was finally ended after 1947 by the **East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (জমিদারি প্রথা উচ্ছেদ)**.

| Period | Movement | Leader / key person |

| c. 1760–1800 | **ফকির-সন্ন্যাসী বিদ্রোহ** | **মজনু শাহ** (Fakir leader), **ভবানী পাঠক** |
| 1818 onward | **ফরায়েজি আন্দোলন** | **হাজী শরীয়তউল্লাহ**, then his son **দুদু মিয়া** |
| 1831 | **Titumir's revolt; বাঁশের কেল্লা** | **তিতুমীর** |
| 1857 | **Sepoy Revolt (সিপাহি বিদ্রোহ)** | **মঙ্গল পান্ডে** and others |
| 1859–1860 | **নীল বিদ্রোহ (Indigo revolt)** | Indigo peasants; **দীনবন্ধু মিত্র** wrote "নীলদর্পণ" |

## Titumir (তিতুমীর) 🔥
- Real name **সৈয়দ মীর নিসার আলী**; born in **1782** at **Chandpur (বারাসাত), 24 Parganas**, West Bengal.
- He was influenced by **সৈয়দ আহমদ বেরেলভী**'s reform movement (তরিকা-ই-মুহাম্মদিয়া).
- He fought against oppressive **zamindars and indigo planters** (a local zamindar even imposed a tax on beards — "দাড়ির খাজনা").
- He built the famous **বাঁশের কেল্লা (bamboo fort)** at **নারকেলবাড়িয়া** in **1831**.
- He was killed fighting British troops on **19 November 1831**; the fort was destroyed by cannon.

## Faraizi movement (ফরায়েজি আন্দোলন) 🔥
- Founder: **হাজী শরীয়তউল্লাহ** (born **1781**, **শামাইল, Madaripur**). He started it after returning from Makkah, in **1818** (some sources: 1820).
- "Faraiz" = compulsory religious duties. It aimed to purify Muslim society and also stood up for peasants.
- His son **দুদু মিয়া (মুহসীনউদ্দীন আহমদ)** turned it into an organised **peasant movement** against zamindars and indigo planters. He declared **"জমির মালিক আল্লাহ"** — land belongs to God, so no one may charge rent on it.

## Indigo revolt (নীল বিদ্রোহ) 🔥
- European planters forced peasants to grow indigo on bad terms (**দাদন** advance system) and tortured those who refused.
- The great revolt of **1859–1860** spread across Bengal.
- 🔥 **"নীলদর্পণ" (1860)**, a play by **দীনবন্ধু মিত্র**, showed the planters' cruelty. It was translated into English (commonly credited to **মাইকেল মধুসূদন দত্ত**) and published by **Rev. James Long**, who was fined and jailed.
- **হরিশচন্দ্র মুখোপাধ্যায়**'s paper **"হিন্দু প্যাট্রিয়ট"** supported the peasants.
- The Government formed the **Indigo Commission (1860)**; forced indigo cultivation declined.

## Sepoy Revolt of 1857 (সিপাহি বিদ্রোহ) 🔥
- Immediate cause: the new **Enfield rifle cartridges**, rumoured to be greased with cow and pig fat. Deeper causes: **Doctrine of Lapse (স্বত্ববিলোপ নীতি)** of **Lord Dalhousie**, economic exploitation, discrimination against Indian sepoys.
- 🔥 Began at **ব্যারাকপুর**: sepoy **মঙ্গল পান্ডে** revolted on **29 March 1857** (he was hanged).
- Large-scale revolt broke out at **মিরাট on 10 May 1857**; rebels marched to Delhi and declared **বাহাদুর শাহ জাফর** emperor.
- Other leaders: **Rani Lakshmibai** (Jhansi), **Nana Sahib**, **Tantia Tope**.
- In **Chattogram**, sepoys revolted under **হাবিলদার রজব আলী**.

- **Bahadur Shah Zafar** — the **last Mughal emperor** — was exiled to **রেঙ্গুন (Yangon)**, where he died (1862).
- **Results:** **Government of India Act 1858**: Company rule ended; India came under the **British Crown**. **Lord Canning** became the **first Viceroy**.

BD-07.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams repeat: who partitioned Bengal (Curzon, 1905), when it was annulled (1911), where the Muslim League was founded (Dhaka, 1906), who moved the Lahore Resolution (A. K. Fazlul Huq) and the dates of 1947.

## Partition of Bengal 1905 (বঙ্গভঙ্গ) 🔥
- Done by Viceroy **লর্ড কার্জন**; took effect on **16 October 1905**.
- New province: **"পূর্ববঙ্গ ও আসাম" (Eastern Bengal and Assam)**, capital **ঢাকা**. First Lieutenant-Governor: **Sir Bampfylde Fuller**.
- Official reason: the old Bengal Presidency was too large to govern. Muslims of East Bengal generally **welcomed** it (new opportunities); many Hindu leaders **opposed** it.
- Opposition grew into the **স্বদেশী আন্দোলন** (boycott of British goods). Rabindranath Tagore wrote **"আমার সোনার বাংলা"** during this movement (1905).
- 🔥 **Annulled (বঙ্গভঙ্গ রদ): 12 December 1911**, announced by **King George V** at the **Delhi Durbar**. The capital of India moved from **Calcutta to Delhi** (1911 announcement; formally 1912).
- As compensation to East Bengal Muslims, the Government promised a university at Dhaka → **University of Dhaka (1921)**.

## All-India Muslim League 🔥
- **Simla Deputation (1 October 1906):** a Muslim delegation led by **স্যার আগা খান (তৃতীয়)** met Viceroy **Lord Minto** and asked for separate electorates.
- 🔥 **Founded 30 December 1906** at **ঢাকা** (**Shahbagh / Ahsan Manzil**, during the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference). The proposal came from **নবাব স্যার সলিমুল্লাহ**. The session was chaired by **নবাব ভিকার-উল-মুলক**; **Sir Aga Khan III** became the first (permanent) president.
- **Morley–Minto Reform (1909):** gave Muslims a **separate electorate**.
- **Lucknow Pact (1916):** Congress–League agreement.
- **Khilafat and Non-cooperation movements (1919–1922).**
- **Bengal Pact (1923):** by **চিত্তরঞ্জন দাশ (C. R. Das)**, promising Muslims a fair share of jobs.

## 1930s–1940s in Bengal
- **Government of India Act 1935** → provincial elections **1937**. **এ. কে. ফজলুল হক** ("শেরে বাংলা"), leader of the **কৃষক প্রজা পার্টি**, became **Prime Minister of Bengal** in a coalition with the Muslim League. His government set up **ঋণ সালিশি বোর্ড** (debt settlement boards).
- The word **"Pakistan"** was coined by **চৌধুরী রহমত আলী** (1933).
- **Two-nation theory (দ্বিজাতি তত্ত্ব):** Hindus and Muslims are two separate nations. Put forward politically by **মুহম্মদ আলী জিন্নাহ** (the idea goes back to Syed Ahmad Khan and Allama Iqbal).

## Lahore Resolution 1940 (লাহোর প্রস্তাব) 🔥🔥
- Adopted at the Muslim League session in **Lahore**, **23 March 1940** (session 22–24 March), chaired by **Jinnah**.
- 🔥 Moved by **এ. কে. ফজলুল হক**.
- It demanded independent **"States"** (plural) for the Muslim-majority areas in the north-west and east of India.
- **Delhi Convention (April 1946):** the Muslim League legislators changed "States" to **one "State"**; the amendment was moved by **হোসেন শহীদ সোহরাওয়ার্দী**.
- Later, the Bengali leaders of 1966–71 argued that the original Lahore Resolution supported autonomy for East Bengal (the **Six-point** demand refers to it).

## Road to 1947 (timeline) 🔥
| Year | Event | Key person |
|---|---|---|
| 1942 | Cripps Mission; **Quit India movement** (Congress) | Stafford Cripps, Gandhi |
| 1943 | **পঞ্চাশের মন্বন্তর** (Bengal famine, Bangla 1350) | — |
| 1946 | **Cabinet Mission** plan | — |
| 1946 | Suhrawardy becomes **Prime Minister of Bengal** | H. S. Suhrawardy |
| 16 Aug 1946 | **Direct Action Day**; Calcutta riots | Muslim League |
| 1947 | **United independent Bengal** proposal (failed) | **Suhrawardy, আবুল হাশিম, শরৎচন্দ্র বসু** |
| 3 June 1947 | **Mountbatten Plan** (partition plan) | **Lord Mountbatten** (last Viceroy) |
| July 1947 | **Sylhet referendum** — Sylhet joined East Bengal (except Karimganj) | — |
| July 1947 | **Indian Independence Act** passed by British Parliament | — |
| **14 Aug 1947** | **Pakistan** independent | Jinnah (Governor-General), **Liaquat Ali Khan** (first PM) |
| **15 Aug 1947** | **India** independent | Nehru (first PM) |

- Boundaries were drawn by the **Radcliffe Commission** (Sir Cyril Radcliffe) — the **Radcliffe Line**.
- East Bengal (পূর্ব বাংলা) became the eastern wing of Pakistan, separated from the west wing by about 1,600 km of India. **Khawaja Nazimuddin** became its first Chief Minister.

## Quick revision
- Partition of Bengal: **Lord Curzon**, effective **16 October 1905**; capital of new province **Dhaka**.
- Annulled: **12 December 1911**, Delhi Durbar, **King George V**.
- Muslim League: **30 December 1906, Dhaka**; proposed by **Nawab Salimullah**; first president **Aga Khan III**.
- Separate electorate: **Morley–Minto Reform 1909**.
- Lahore Resolution: **23 March 1940**, moved by **A. K. Fazlul Huq**; "States".
- "States" → "State": **Delhi Convention 1946**, moved by **Suhrawardy**.
- Name "Pakistan": **Chowdhury Rahmat Ali**.
- Last Viceroy: **Mountbatten**; plan **3 June 1947**.
- Pakistan **14 August**, India **15 August 1947**.

BD-08.notes:
> **Why it matters:** One of the most-asked Bangladesh topics: Tamaddun Majlish, Dhirendranath Datta's proposal, Jinnah's declaration, 21 February 1952 (8 Falgun 1358), the martyrs, the Shaheed Minar and UNESCO's recognition.

## Background
- Pakistan's rulers wanted **Urdu** as the only state language, though **Bangla** was the mother tongue of about **56%** of Pakistan's people.
- 🔥 **তমদ্দুন মজলিশ** was founded on **1 September 1947** by **Prof. আবুল কাশেম** (Dhaka University). It was the **first organisation** of the Language Movement.
- On **15 September 1947** it published the booklet **"পাকিস্তানের রাষ্ট্রভাষা: বাংলা না উর্দু?"**.
- The first **রাষ্ট্রভাষা সংগ্রাম পরিষদ** was formed in October 1947 (convener **নুরুল হক ভূঁইয়া**).

## Phase 1 — 1948 🔥
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| **25 Feb 1948** | 🔥 **ধীরেন্দ্রনাথ দত্ত** (Cumilla) demanded in the **Pakistan Constituent Assembly** that Bangla also be used as a language of the Assembly. It was rejected |
| 2 Mar 1948 | The Sangram Parishad was re-formed (convener **শামসুল আলম**) |
| **11 Mar 1948** | First **general strike (হরতাল)** for the state language; **Sheikh Mujibur Rahman**, Shamsul Haque and others arrested |
| 15 Mar 1948 | Chief Minister **খাজা নাজিমউদ্দিন** signed an **8-point agreement** with the Sangram Parishad |
| **21 Mar 1948** | 🔥 **জিন্নাহ**, at the **Race Course (রেসকোর্স) meeting**, declared: **"Urdu and only Urdu shall be the state language of Pakistan"** |
| **24 Mar 1948** | He repeated it at the **Dhaka University convocation (Curzon Hall)**; students shouted **"No, no"** |

## Phase 2 — 1952 🔥🔥
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| **27 Jan 1952** | Pakistan PM **খাজা নাজিমউদ্দিন**, at **Paltan**, again declared Urdu the only state language |
| **31 Jan 1952** | 🔥 **সর্বদলীয় কেন্দ্রীয় রাষ্ট্রভাষা সংগ্রাম পরিষদ** formed, chaired by **মওলানা আবদুল হামিদ খান ভাসানী**; convener **কাজী গোলাম মাহবুব** |
| 20 Feb 1952 | The **Nurul Amin** government (Chief Minister of East Bengal) imposed **Section 144** in Dhaka |
| **21 Feb 1952** | Students met at the **আমতলা** of Dhaka University (meeting chaired by **গাজীউল হক**) and decided to **break Section 144**. Police fired near **Dhaka Medical College**. Date in Bangla: **৮ ফাল্গুন ১৩৫৮** |
| 22 Feb 1952 | More killings during a mourning procession (Shafiur Rahman, child **Ohiullah**) |
| 23 Feb 1952 | Students built the **first Shaheed Minar** overnight; police **demolished it on 26 Feb** |

### Martyrs (ভাষা শহীদ) 🔥
- **রফিক উদ্দিন আহমদ** (commonly called the **first martyr**), **আবুল বরকত**, **আবদুল জব্বার** (21 Feb)
- **আবদুস সালাম** (wounded on 21 Feb, died **7 April 1952**)
- **শফিউর রহমান** (22 Feb), and the child **অহিউল্লাহ**
## Recognition 🔥
- The **1956 constitution** of Pakistan made **Bangla and Urdu** state languages (**Article 214**).
- The present **Central Shaheed Minar** was designed by **হামিদুর রহমান** (with sculptor **নভেরা আহমেদ**). It was inaugurated on **21 February 1963** by **হাসিনা বেগম**, mother of martyr Abul Barkat.
- 🔥 **UNESCO** declared **21 February** the **International Mother Language Day** on **17 November 1999**; it was first observed in **2000**. The initiative came from Canada-based expatriates **রফিকুল ইসলাম** and **আবদুস সালাম** (Mother Language Lovers of the World).
- **Sierra Leone** declared Bangla an **honorary official language** in **2002** (for the role of Bangladeshi UN peacekeepers).
- The **Ekushey Padak (একুশে পদক)**, the second-highest civilian award, was introduced in **1976**.

## Literature of the Language Movement 🔥
| Work | Writer |
|---|---|
| Song **"আমার ভাইয়ের রক্তে রাঙানো একুশে ফেব্রুয়ারি"** | Lyrics **আবদুল গাফফার চৌধুরী**; present tune **আলতাফ মাহমুদ** (first tune by Abdul Latif) |
| First poem **"কাঁদতে আসিনি ফাঁসির দাবি নিয়ে এসেছি"** | **মাহবুব উল আলম চৌধুরী** (Chattogram) |
| Play **"কবর"** (written in jail, 1953) | **মুনীর চৌধুরী** |
| Novel **"আরেক ফাল্গুন"** | **জহির রায়হান** |
| Compilation **"একুশে ফেব্রুয়ারি"** (1953) | Edited by **হাসান হাফিজুর রহমান** |

## Quick revision
- First organisation: **Tamaddun Majlish** (1 Sept 1947), **Prof. Abul Kashem**.
- Constituent Assembly demand: **Dhirendranath Datta**, **25 Feb 1948**.
- First language strike: **11 March 1948**.
- Jinnah's "Urdu only": **21 March 1948** (Race Course), **24 March** (Curzon Hall).
- All-Party Sangram Parishad: **31 Jan 1952**, chair **Bhashani**, convener **Kazi Golam Mahboob**.
- Section 144 imposed by the **Nurul Amin** government.
- 21 Feb 1952 = **8 Falgun 1358**.
- Shaheed Minar designer: **Hamidur Rahman**; inaugurated **21 Feb 1963**.
- UNESCO recognition: **17 November 1999**; first observed **2000**.
- Bangla a state language of Pakistan: **1956 constitution, Art. 214**.

BD-09.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask about the Awami Muslim League's founding, the United Front and its 21 points, the "boat" symbol, the 1956 and 1962 constitutions, Ayub Khan's martial law and Basic Democracy, and 17 September (Education Day).

## Awami Muslim League (1949) 🔥
- Founded **23 June 1949** at **রোজ গার্ডেন, Dhaka**.
- President **মওলানা আবদুল হামিদ খান ভাসানী**; General Secretary **শামসুল হক**; one of the Joint Secretaries **শেখ মুজিবুর রহমান** (then in jail).
- The word "Muslim" was dropped in **1955** → **Awami League** (open to all communities).

## 1954 provincial election and the United Front 🔥🔥
- **যুক্তফ্রন্ট (United Front)** was formed on **4 December 1953** by four parties:

| Party | Leader |
|---|---|
| **আওয়ামী মুসলিম লীগ** | মওলানা ভাসানী |
| **কৃষক শ্রমিক পার্টি** | **এ. কে. ফজলুল হক** |
| **নেজামে ইসলাম** | মওলানা আতাহার আলী |
| **গণতন্ত্রী দল** | হাজী মোহাম্মদ দানেশ |

- Election symbol: **নৌকা (boat)**. Manifesto: **২১ দফা (21-point programme)** — the first point was **Bangla as a state language**; others included autonomy for East Bengal, 21 February as a holiday and a Shaheed Minar.
- Election held in **March 1954**. The United Front won a **landslide**: about **223** of the 237 Muslim seats (some books give a slightly different total). The ruling **Muslim League got only 9 seats**.
- **A. K. Fazlul Huq** became **Chief Minister** of East Bengal (April 1954).
- The central government **dismissed** the ministry on **30 May 1954** and imposed **Governor's rule (Section 92A)**; **Iskander Mirza** was made Governor.

## 1956 constitution 🔥
- The **first constitution of Pakistan**; adopted **29 February 1956**, effective **23 March 1956**.
- Pakistan became the **"Islamic Republic of Pakistan"**; **parliamentary** system; **unicameral** legislature with **parity** between the two wings.
- **Bangla and Urdu** were both made state languages (**Article 214**).
- The **One Unit** scheme (October 1955) had merged the western provinces into **West Pakistan**; East Bengal came to be called **East Pakistan (পূর্ব পাকিস্তান)** (the name is dated to 1955 in some books and to the 1956 constitution in others).
- **Iskander Mirza** became the **first President** of Pakistan under it.
- **Kagmari Conference (February 1957):** Bhashani warned West Pakistan with his famous **"আসসালামু আলাইকুম"** (farewell) if East Pakistan's demands were ignored. He later formed the **National Awami Party (NAP)** in **1957**.

## 1958 martial law 🔥
- Violence in the East Pakistan Assembly: **Deputy Speaker শাহেদ আলী** was injured in the House and died (September 1958).
- **7 October 1958:** President **Iskander Mirza** abrogated the constitution and declared **martial law**; **General আইয়ুব খান** became Chief Martial Law Administrator.
- **27 October 1958:** Ayub removed Mirza and became **President** — Pakistan's **first military ruler**.

### Basic Democracy (মৌলিক গণতন্ত্র), 1959
- Ayub's system of **80,000 "Basic Democrats"** (**40,000 in each wing**), elected locally. They formed the **electoral college** for the President and the assemblies.
- Ayub was confirmed by a referendum of Basic Democrats in **1960**.

## 1962 constitution and movement 🔥
- **Second constitution** of Pakistan: promulgated **1 March 1962**, effective **8 June 1962**.
- **Presidential** system; **indirect election** of the President through the Basic Democrats. It concentrated power in the President.
- Protests against Ayub's rule and the constitution were led by students.
- 🔥 **শিক্ষা আন্দোলন (Education Movement) 1962:** against the **Sharif Commission** report on education. Police firing on **17 September 1962** killed students. **17 September is observed as শিক্ষা দিবস (Education Day)**.
- **1965:** Ayub defeated **ফাতেমা জিন্নাহ** in the presidential election (through Basic Democrats). The **17-day Indo-Pak war (1965)** showed that East Pakistan had been left undefended.

## Timeline
| Date | Event | Key person |
|---|---|---|
| 23 June 1949 | Awami Muslim League founded | Bhashani, Shamsul Huq, Mujib |
| 4 Dec 1953 | United Front formed | Huq, Bhashani, Suhrawardy |
| March 1954 | Provincial election; United Front landslide | Fazlul Huq (CM) |
| 30 May 1954 | Huq ministry dismissed; Section 92A | Iskander Mirza (Governor) |
| 23 Mar 1956 | First constitution in force | — |
| Feb 1957 | Kagmari Conference | Bhashani |
| 7 Oct 1958 | Martial law | Iskander Mirza, Ayub Khan |
| 27 Oct 1958 | Ayub takes over as President | Ayub Khan |
| 1959 | Basic Democracy | Ayub Khan |
| 8 June 1962 | Second constitution in force | Ayub Khan |
| 17 Sep 1962 | Education Movement martyrs | — |

## Quick revision
- Awami Muslim League: **23 June 1949**, **Rose Garden**; president **Bhashani**.
- United Front: **4 parties**; symbol **boat**; **21 points**.
- 1954: Muslim League won just **9** seats; **Fazlul Huq** Chief Minister; dismissed under **92A**.
- 1956 constitution: in force **23 March 1956**; Bangla + Urdu state languages (**Art. 214**).
- First President of Pakistan: **Iskander Mirza**.
- Martial law: **7 October 1958**; Ayub President from **27 October 1958**.
- Basic Democrats: **80,000** (40,000 per wing).
- 1962 constitution: **presidential**, in force **8 June 1962**.
- Education Day: **17 September** (1962, Sharif Commission).

> **Why it matters:** Standard questions: where and when the Six-point was placed, its nickname ("Magna Carta"), 7 June, the Agartala case (accused no. 1, Sergeant Zahurul Haq), the 11-point programme, Asad and Matiur, and who gave the title "Bangabandhu".

## Six-point programme (ছয় দফা) 🔥🔥
- Placed by **শেখ মুজিবুর রহমান** at a conference of opposition parties in **লাহোর** on **5 February 1966**.
- Called the **"বাঙালির মুক্তির সনদ" (Charter of Freedom)** and the **"Magna Carta of the Bengalis"**.
- It was based on the spirit of the **Lahore Resolution (1940)** and demanded **full autonomy** for East Pakistan.

| Point | Demand (in short) |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Federal, parliamentary government** on the basis of the Lahore Resolution; direct elections by adult franchise; supreme legislature |
| 2 | Federal (central) government to deal only with **defence and foreign affairs** |
| 3 | **Two separate but freely convertible currencies**, or one currency with measures to stop capital flight from East to West |
| 4 | **Power of taxation** and revenue collection with the federating units (provinces) |
| 5 | **Separate foreign-exchange accounts** for the two wings; provinces free to make trade links abroad |
| 6 | A separate **militia or paramilitary force** for East Pakistan |

- 🔥 **7 June 1966:** a general strike for the Six-point; police firing killed several people including worker **মনু মিয়া** (Tejgaon). **7 June = ছয় দফা দিবস**.
- Mujib and many leaders were arrested.

## Agartala Conspiracy Case (আগরতলা ষড়যন্ত্র মামলা) 🔥
- Official name: **"রাষ্ট্র বনাম শেখ মুজিবুর রহমান ও অন্যান্য" (State vs. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and others)**.
- Charge: conspiring with India (at **Agartala**, Tripura) to make East Pakistan independent by armed revolt.
- **35 accused**; 🔥 **Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was accused no. 1**.
- Case filed in **January 1968**; trial began on **19 June 1968** in a special tribunal at **Kurmitola cantonment**, Dhaka.
- 🔥 Accused **সার্জেন্ট জহুরুল হক** was **shot dead in custody on 15 February 1969**. (Dhaka University's Iqbal Hall was later renamed **জহুরুল হক হল**.)
- Under the pressure of the mass uprising, the Government **withdrew the case on 22 February 1969** and released all accused.

## 1969 mass uprising (উনসত্তরের গণঅভ্যুত্থান) 🔥
- **ছাত্র সংগ্রাম পরিষদ** (Students' Action Committee) announced the **১১ দফা (11-point programme)** in **January 1969**. It included the Six-point demands plus student and peasant–worker demands.
- 🔥 **20 January 1969:** student leader **আসাদ (আমানুল্লাহ মোহাম্মদ আসাদুজ্জামান)** was killed by police; **Ayub Gate** was renamed **আসাদ গেট**. Poet **শামসুর রাহমান** wrote **"আসাদের শার্ট"**.
- 🔥 **24 January 1969:** school student **মতিউর রহমান** was killed. **24 January is observed as গণঅভ্যুত্থান দিবস**.
- **18 February 1969:** **Dr. শামসুজ্জোহা**, proctor of **Rajshahi University**, was killed by the army while protecting students — often called the **first martyred intellectual (teacher)** of the independence struggle.
- **22 February 1969:** Agartala case withdrawn; Mujib released.
- 🔥 **23 February 1969:** at a huge reception at the **Race Course**, Mujib was given the title **"বঙ্গবন্ধু"**. The title was announced by **তোফায়েল আহমেদ**, **DUCSU VP** and leader of the Students' Action Committee.
- **25 March 1969:** **Ayub Khan resigned**; General **ইয়াহিয়া খান** took power and imposed **martial law**.

## After the uprising
- **5 December 1969:** at a meeting remembering Suhrawardy, Bangabandhu said East Pakistan would be called **"বাংলাদেশ"**.
- Yahya issued the **Legal Framework Order (LFO)** on **30 March 1970** for elections and abolished **One Unit** (1 July 1970). Elections were announced on the basis of **population (one person, one vote)** — which gave East Pakistan a majority of seats (see BD-11).

BD-11.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask the seat numbers of the 1970 election (160/162, 167/169, 288/300), the two non-Awami League winners, the events of 1–3 March 1971, and facts about the 7 March speech (place, length, UNESCO recognition).

## 1970 general election 🔥🔥
- Held under **Yahya Khan's Legal Framework Order (LFO)**, on the basis of **population**.
- **National Assembly:** **7 December 1970**. **Provincial Assembly:** **17 December 1970**.
- The **Bhola cyclone of 12 November 1970** (one of the deadliest cyclones in history) delayed polling in some coastal seats to January 1971.
- Awami League's symbol: **নৌকা (boat)**; it campaigned on the **Six-point**.

### National Assembly results
| | Total | East Pakistan | Awami League won |
|---|---|---|---|
| General seats | **300** | **162** | 🔥 **160** |
| Reserved women's seats | 13 | 7 | 7 |
| Total | **313** | **169** | 🔥 **167** |

- The Awami League won an **absolute majority** of the whole National Assembly (167 of 313) — although it won **no seat in West Pakistan**.
- 🔥 The two East Pakistan general seats **not** won by the Awami League went to **নুরুল আমিন** (PDP) and **রাজা ত্রিদিব রায়** (Chakma chief, independent).
- **জুলফিকার আলী ভুট্টো**'s **Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP)** came second with **81** general seats (all in the West; 88 with women's seats).

### East Pakistan Provincial Assembly results
- Total **310** seats (300 general + 10 women). 🔥 Awami League won **288 general** + **10 women's** = **298**.

## From victory to non-cooperation (March 1971) 🔥
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| **1 March 1971** | Yahya **postponed** the National Assembly session (due on 3 March) → spontaneous protests |
| **2 March 1971** | 🔥 The **first flag of independent Bangladesh** was hoisted at the **Kala Bhaban (বটতলা), Dhaka University** by **আ স ম আবদুর রব** (DUCSU VP) |
| **3 March 1971** | **স্বাধীন বাংলা ছাত্র সংগ্রাম পরিষদ** read the **Manifesto of Independence (স্বাধীনতার ইশতেহার)** at **Paltan** (read by **শাজাহান সিরাজ**); "আমার সোনার বাংলা" was named the national anthem and Bangabandhu the leader of the movement |
| **7 March 1971** | Bangabandhu's historic speech at the Race Course |
| 16–24 March | Mujib–Yahya talks (Bhutto also joined) |
| **23 March 1971** | Observed as **প্রতিরোধ দিবস**; the Bangladesh flag was flown across the province, including at Bangabandhu's house (Dhanmondi 32) |
| 25 March 1971 | Talks collapse; **Operation Searchlight** (see BD-12) |

## The 7 March speech (৭ই মার্চের ভাষণ) 🔥🔥
- Place: **রেসকোর্স ময়দান** (now **সোহরাওয়ার্দী উদ্যান**), Dhaka.
- Length: about **18–19 minutes** (commonly **18 minutes**); about **1,100 words**.
- 🔥 Key line: **"এবারের সংগ্রাম আমাদের মুক্তির সংগ্রাম, এবারের সংগ্রাম স্বাধীনতার সংগ্রাম।"**
- Other famous lines: **"ঘরে ঘরে দুর্গ গড়ে তোলো"**, **"রক্ত যখন দিয়েছি, রক্ত আরও দেবো…"**.
- It announced a **non-cooperation movement** and put **four conditions** before joining the Assembly:
  1. **Withdraw martial law**
  2. **Send the army back to the barracks**
  3. **Inquire into the killings**
  4. **Hand over power to the elected representatives**
- 🔥 **UNESCO** listed the speech in its **Memory of the World International Register** on **30 October 2017** (documentary heritage).
- The speech was placed in the **Fifth Schedule** of the Constitution by the **15th amendment (2011)**.
- *Newsweek* (April 1971) called Bangabandhu the **"Poet of Politics"**.

> 🔄 Update: the list of national days and some constitutional provisions linked to this period (including the schedules) were revised or proposed for reform after August 2024. Check the current position before the exam.

## Quick revision
- Election dates: NA **7 Dec 1970**; PA **17 Dec 1970**.
- AL: **160/162** general seats in East; **167/313** in total NA.
- Non-AL winners in East: **Nurul Amin** and **Raja Tridiv Roy**.
- Provincial: AL **288** general + 10 women = **298/310**.
- PPP (Bhutto): **81** general seats.
- First flag hoisted: **2 March 1971**, **A. S. M. Abdur Rab**, DU Kala Bhaban.
- Manifesto of Independence: **3 March 1971**, Paltan, read by **Shahjahan Siraj**.
- 7 March speech: Race Course; ~**18 minutes**; **4 demands**.
- UNESCO Memory of the World: **30 October 2017**.

BD-12.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Very frequently asked: the night of 25 March, the first resistance (Rajarbagh), the declaration of independence and Kalurghat radio, the Proclamation of Independence (10 April), the oath at Baidyanathtala (17 April) and the ministers of the Mujibnagar Government.

## Operation Searchlight (অপারেশন সার্চলাইট) 🔥🔥
- The Pakistan army's planned crackdown on the night of **25 March 1971**.
- Planned by **General টিক্কা খান** and **Major General রাও ফরমান আলী** (with Maj. Gen. Khadim Hussain Raja). Tikka Khan is remembered as the **"Butcher of Bengal"**.
- Main targets in Dhaka:
  - **Dhaka University** — **জগন্নাথ হল**, **ইকবাল হল** (now Zahurul Haq Hall), teachers' quarters. Teachers killed that night included **ড. গোবিন্দচন্দ্র দেব** and **জ্যোতির্ময় গুহঠাকুরতা** (died of wounds).
  - 🔥 **রাজারবাগ পুলিশ লাইন্স** — the police put up the **first armed resistance** of the Liberation War.
  - **পিলখানা** (EPR headquarters).
- Foreign journalist **সাইমন ড্রিং** (*Daily Telegraph*) hid in Dhaka and reported the massacre to the world. **Anthony Mascarenhas**'s article **"Genocide"** (*Sunday Times*, June 1971) also exposed it.
- 🔥 In 2017 the Jatiya Sangsad declared **25 March** as **গণহত্যা দিবস (Genocide Day)**.

## Declaration of independence 🔥🔥
- In the early hours of **26 March 1971**, before his arrest, **বঙ্গবন্ধু শেখ মুজিবুর রহমান** declared the independence of Bangladesh; the message was sent out by wireless (EPR). He was then **arrested** and flown to West Pakistan, where he was imprisoned and put on trial.
- **26 March = স্বাধীনতা দিবস (Independence Day).**
- 🔥 On **26 March**, Awami League leader **এম. এ. হান্নান** (Chattogram) read the declaration on the radio from **কালুরঘাট (Chattogram)**.
- The radio became **স্বাধীন বাংলা বেতার কেন্দ্র**. On **27 March 1971**, **Major জিয়াউর রহমান** read a declaration of independence from Kalurghat **on behalf of Bangabandhu**.
- The Constitution (after the 15th amendment, 2011) records Bangabandhu's declaration telegram in its **Sixth Schedule**.
- Swadhin Bangla Betar later broadcast from Kolkata. Famous programmes: **"চরমপত্র"** (**এম. আর. আখতার মুকুল**) and **"জল্লাদের দরবার"**.

> Note: Who "declared" independence has been a politically debated question. For exams, give the answers above: Bangabandhu's declaration on 26 March; M. A. Hannan's broadcast on 26 March; Ziaur Rahman's broadcast on behalf of Bangabandhu on 27 March.

## Proclamation of Independence (স্বাধীনতার ঘোষণাপত্র) 🔥
- Issued on **10 April 1971** by the elected representatives, at **Mujibnagar**; it gave the new government legal basis and took effect **from 26 March 1971**.
- It is sometimes called the **first (interim) constitution** of Bangladesh. It now forms the **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution (15th amendment).

## Mujibnagar Government (মুজিবনগর সরকার) 🔥🔥
- **Formed: 10 April 1971.** **Oath: 17 April 1971** at the mango grove of **বৈদ্যনাথতলা, মেহেরপুর** — renamed **মুজিবনগর**. The **first government of Bangladesh**.
- The oath was administered and the Proclamation read by **অধ্যাপক ইউসুফ আলী** (MNA).
- **17 April = মুজিবনগর দিবস**.
- Its headquarters and secretariat worked from **8 Theatre Road, Kolkata**.

|---|---|
| **President** | **বঙ্গবন্ধু শেখ মুজিবুর রহমান** (in Pakistani jail) |
| **Vice-President & Acting President** | 🔥 **সৈয়দ নজরুল ইসলাম** |
| **Prime Minister** | 🔥 **তাজউদ্দীন আহমদ** (first PM of Bangladesh) |
| Foreign Affairs & Law | **খন্দকার মোশতাক আহমদ** |
| Finance | **এম. মনসুর আলী** |
| Home, Relief & Rehabilitation | **এ. এইচ. এম. কামারুজ্জামান** |
| **Commander-in-Chief** | **কর্নেল (অব.) এম. এ. জি. ওসমানী** |

- Main tasks: running the war (sectors, forces), diplomacy abroad, caring for **about 1 crore refugees** in India, and broadcasting through Swadhin Bangla Betar.

BD-13.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams love the sector table (which sector had no commander, which covered Dhaka, Z/K/S forces), the Bir Sreshtho list (place of death, youngest, only Air Force/Navy member) and the number of gallantry awards.

## Sectors (সেক্টর) 🔥
- For the war, Bangladesh was divided into **11 sectors**, decided at the **sector commanders' conference in Kolkata, July 1971**.
- 🔥 **Sector 10** had **no fixed area and no regular commander**: it was the **naval commando** sector (rivers and sea ports), under the **Commander-in-Chief** directly.
- Each sector had sub-sectors; the fighters were regular soldiers (**নিয়মিত বাহিনী**) and guerrillas (**গণবাহিনী / Freedom Fighters**).

| Sector | Main area | Commander(s) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Chattogram, Chattogram Hill Tracts, east Noakhali | **Major জিয়াউর রহমান**, then **Major রফিকুল ইসলাম** |
| 2 | Dhaka, Cumilla, Faridpur, part of Noakhali | 🔥 **Major খালেদ মোশাররফ**, then **Major এ. টি. এম. হায়দার** |
| 3 | Brahmanbaria, Habiganj, Kishoreganj, part of Dhaka | **Major কে. এম. সফিউল্লাহ**, then **Major এ. এন. এম. নূরুজ্জামান** |
| 4 | North-east Sylhet (Moulvibazar side) | **Major সি. আর. দত্ত** |
| 5 | North-west Sylhet (Sunamganj side) | **Major মীর শওকত আলী** |
| 6 | Rangpur, part of Dinajpur | **Wing Commander এম. খাদেমুল বাশার** |
| 7 | Rajshahi, Pabna, Bogura, part of Dinajpur | **Major নাজমুল হক**, then **Major কাজী নূরুজ্জামান** |
| 8 | Kushtia, Jashore, part of Khulna and Faridpur | **Major আবু ওসমান চৌধুরী**, then **Major এম. এ. মঞ্জুর** |
| 9 | Barishal, Patuakhali, part of Khulna | **Major এম. এ. জলিল**, then others |
| 10 | Naval commandos (ports and rivers) | No regular commander |
| 11 | Mymensingh, Tangail | **Major আবু তাহের**, then **Squadron Leader এম. হামিদুল্লাহ খান** |

- Sector 6 is often noted as the sector whose headquarters stayed **inside Bangladesh** (Patgram area).

## Forces (বাহিনী) 🔥
### Brigade forces (named after commanders' initials)
| Force | Commander |
|---|---|
| 🔥 **জেড ফোর্স (Z Force)** — first brigade | **Major জিয়াউর রহমান** |
| **কে ফোর্স (K Force)** | **Major খালেদ মোশাররফ** |
| **এস ফোর্স (S Force)** | **Major কে. এম. সফিউল্লাহ** |

### Other forces
- **মুজিব বাহিনী (BLF)** — led by student and youth leaders (Sheikh Fazlul Haque Moni, Serajul Alam Khan, Abdur Razzak, Tofail Ahmed).
- **কাদেরিয়া বাহিনী** — **আবদুল কাদের সিদ্দিকী** (Tangail), "বঙ্গবীর".
- **হেমায়েত বাহিনী** (Gopalganj–Faridpur area) and **আফসার বাহিনী** (Mymensingh area).
- 🔥 **Naval commandos — "অপারেশন জ্যাকপট" (15–16 August 1971):** simultaneous attacks on ships at **Chattogram, Mongla, Chandpur and Narayanganj** ports.
- 🔥 **Bangladesh Air Force — "কিলো ফ্লাইট"**: formed on **28 September 1971** at **Dimapur (Nagaland, India)**; first attack on **3 December 1971** (fuel depots at Narayanganj and Chattogram). Led by Group Captain **A. K. Khandker** (with Squadron Leader Sultan Mahmud).
- 🔥 **Allied / Joint Command (যৌথ বাহিনী)** of Bangladesh and Indian forces formed on **21 November 1971** → **21 November = সশস্ত্র বাহিনী দিবস (Armed Forces Day)**.

| **ফ্লাইট লেফটেন্যান্ট মতিউর রহমান** | **Air Force** | **20 Aug 1971** | Thatta, Sindh (Pakistan) — tried to fly a T-33 trainer ("Bluebird") from Karachi to Bangladesh |

- The remains of **Matiur Rahman** (from Karachi, 2006) and **Hamidur Rahman** (from Tripura, 2007) were brought home and reburied at **Mirpur Martyred Intellectuals' Graveyard**.

BD-14.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask about 16 December (who signed the surrender, where, who represented Bangladesh), 14 December and the martyred intellectuals, the first countries to recognise Bangladesh, and the roles of India, the USSR, the USA and China.

## Final phase of the war
- **3 December 1971:** Pakistan launched air attacks on Indian air bases → India joined the war fully. Bangladesh–India **joint forces (যৌথ বাহিনী / মিত্রবাহিনী)** advanced quickly.
- 🔥 **6 December 1971:** **Bhutan** and **India** recognised Bangladesh. (Bhutan's recognition is commonly counted **first**, a few hours before India's — the usual exam answer.)
- **USA** sent the **Seventh Fleet** (led by the aircraft carrier **USS Enterprise**) towards the Bay of Bengal in support of Pakistan.
- The **USSR vetoed** ceasefire resolutions in the **UN Security Council** that would have helped Pakistan.

## Victory and surrender (বিজয় ও আত্মসমর্পণ) 🔥🔥
- **Date: 16 December 1971** — **বিজয় দিবস (Victory Day)**.
- Place: **রেসকোর্স ময়দান** (now **সোহরাওয়ার্দী উদ্যান**), Dhaka; in the afternoon (commonly **4:31 pm**).
- 🔥 **Instrument of Surrender** signed by:
  - **Lt. Gen. এ. এ. কে. নিয়াজী** — Commander of Pakistan's Eastern Command (surrendered)
  - **Lt. Gen. জগজিৎ সিং অরোরা** — GOC-in-C of India's Eastern Command, commander of the **joint command** (accepted)
- 🔥 **Bangladesh was represented by Group Captain এ. কে. খন্দকার** (Deputy Chief of Staff). **General Osmani was not present.**
- About **93,000** Pakistani soldiers and personnel became prisoners of war.
- 🔥 **Bangabandhu** was released from Pakistani jail and returned to Dhaka on **10 January 1972** (via London and Delhi) — **স্বদেশ প্রত্যাবর্তন দিবস**.
- The Indian army left Bangladesh by **12 March 1972**.

## Martyred intellectuals (শহীদ বুদ্ধিজীবী) 🔥🔥
- Just before defeat, the Pakistan army and its local collaborators — especially the **আল-বদর** force — abducted and killed teachers, doctors, writers and journalists, mainly on **10–14 December 1971**, to cripple the new nation.
- 🔥 **14 December = শহীদ বুদ্ধিজীবী দিবস (Martyred Intellectuals Day).**
- Bodies were found at **রায়েরবাজার বধ্যভূমি** and **মিরপুর**.

| Martyred intellectual | Profession |
|---|---|
| **মুনীর চৌধুরী** | Teacher, playwright ("কবর") |
| **মোফাজ্জল হায়দার চৌধুরী** | Teacher, linguist |
| **শহীদুল্লাহ কায়সার** | Journalist, novelist ("সংশপ্তক") |
| **সিরাজুদ্দীন হোসেন** | Journalist (Ittefaq) |
| **সেলিনা পারভীন** | Journalist (the "শিলালিপি" magazine) |
| **ডা. ফজলে রাব্বী** | Cardiologist |
| **ডা. আলীম চৌধুরী** | Eye specialist |
| **আনোয়ার পাশা** | Teacher, novelist ("রাইফেল রোটি আওরাত") |
| **গিয়াসউদ্দিন আহমদ**, **রাশীদুল হাসান**, **সন্তোষচন্দ্র ভট্টাচার্য** | Dhaka University teachers |

- Killed on **25 March 1971**: **ড. জি. সি. দেব**, **জ্যোতির্ময় গুহঠাকুরতা**. **ধীরেন্দ্রনাথ দত্ত** was killed in Cumilla in March–April 1971.
- Filmmaker **জহির রায়হান** disappeared on **30 January 1972** at Mirpur while searching for his brother **Shahidullah Kaiser**.

### Memorials
| Memorial | Place | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| 🔥 **জাতীয় স্মৃতিসৌধ** | **Savar** | Designed by **সৈয়দ মাইনুল হোসেন**; **7 triangular planes** (seven stages of the freedom struggle) |
| **রায়েরবাজার বধ্যভূমি স্মৃতিসৌধ** | Dhaka | For the martyred intellectuals |
| **শহীদ বুদ্ধিজীবী স্মৃতিসৌধ** | Mirpur, Dhaka | For the martyred intellectuals |

## Foreign role 🔥
| Country / person | Role |
|---|---|
| **India** (PM **ইন্দিরা গান্ধী**) | Sheltered about **1 crore (10 million) refugees**; trained freedom fighters; joined the war on 3 Dec; recognised Bangladesh on 6 Dec |
| **USSR** | Supported Bangladesh; **Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation (9 August 1971)**; vetoes in the UN Security Council |
| **USA** (President **Nixon**, adviser **Kissinger**) | Government supported Pakistan; sent the **Seventh Fleet**. But US Senator **Edward Kennedy** and many Americans supported Bangladesh; Consul-General **Archer Blood** sent the "Blood Telegram" |
| **China** | Supported Pakistan |
| **Bhutan** | First to recognise Bangladesh (6 Dec 1971) |

### Supporters abroad
- 🔥 **Concert for Bangladesh:** **1 August 1971**, **Madison Square Garden, New York**, organised by **জর্জ হ্যারিসন** and **পণ্ডিত রবিশঙ্কর**.
- **Allen Ginsberg**'s poem **"September on Jessore Road"**.
- French writer **André Malraux** offered to fight for Bangladesh.

## Recognition after the war

| Bhutan, India | 6 December 1971 |
| East Germany (GDR) | 11 January 1972 (first from Europe) |
| USSR | 24 January 1972 |
| UK | 4 February 1972 |
| USA | 4 April 1972 |
| **Commonwealth** membership | **18 April 1972** |
| **Pakistan** | **22 February 1974** (at the time of the OIC Lahore summit) |
| **United Nations** membership | 🔥 **17 September 1974** (136th member) |
| Saudi Arabia | 16 August 1975 |
| China | 31 August 1975 |

## Quick revision
- Victory Day: **16 December 1971**, Race Course (Suhrawardy Udyan).
- Surrender signed by **Niazi** (Pakistan) and **Jagjit Singh Aurora** (joint command).
- Bangladesh representative: **Group Captain A. K. Khandker**.
- About **93,000** POWs.
- Martyred Intellectuals Day: **14 December**; killers mainly **Al-Badr**.
- National Memorial, Savar: **Syed Mainul Hossain**.
- First recognition: **Bhutan** (6 Dec 1971), then India the same day.
- USA sent the **Seventh Fleet**; USSR used its **veto** for Bangladesh.
- Concert for Bangladesh: **1 August 1971**, **George Harrison & Ravi Shankar**.
- UN membership: **17 September 1974**, **136th** member.

BD-15.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask dates of the parliamentary elections, the first election (1973), BAKSAL, 15 August and 3 November 1975, the fall of Ershad (1990), the caretaker system, and the first woman Prime Minister. Keep answers factual and date-based.

## 1972–1975
| Date | Event | Key person |
|---|---|---|
| 10 Jan 1972 | Bangabandhu returns home | Sheikh Mujibur Rahman |
| 11 Jan 1972 | **Provisional Constitution Order** — parliamentary system | — |
| 12 Jan 1972 | Mujib becomes **Prime Minister**; **Justice Abu Sayeed Chowdhury** becomes President | — |
| 4 Nov 1972 | Constitution adopted; in force **16 Dec 1972** | Dr. Kamal Hossain (drafting committee) |
| 🔥 **7 Mar 1973** | **First parliamentary election** — Awami League won **293 of 300** seats | — |
| 1974 | Famine; **state of emergency** declared (28 Dec 1974) | — |
| 🔥 25 Jan 1975 | **4th amendment**: presidential system and one-party rule; Mujib becomes President | — |
| 24 Feb 1975 | **বাকশাল (Bangladesh Krishak Sramik Awami League)** formed as the single national party | — |

## 1975: a year of coups 🔥🔥
- **15 August 1975:** a group of army officers assassinated **Bangabandhu** and most of his family at **Dhanmondi 32**. His daughters **Sheikh Hasina** and **Sheikh Rehana** survived because they were abroad. **খন্দকার মোশতাক আহমদ** became President.
- **26 September 1975:** the **Indemnity Ordinance** barred trial of the killers. (It was repealed in **1996**; the killers were later tried and several executed.)
- 🔥 **3 November 1975 — জেল হত্যা:** four national leaders — **সৈয়দ নজরুল ইসলাম, তাজউদ্দীন আহমদ, এম. মনসুর আলী, এ. এইচ. এম. কামারুজ্জামান** — were killed inside **Dhaka Central Jail**. The same day **Brigadier Khaled Mosharraf** led a counter-coup.
- **6 November 1975:** Chief Justice **আবু সাদাত মোহাম্মদ সায়েম** became President (and Chief Martial Law Administrator).
- **7 November 1975:** a soldiers' uprising freed **Major General জিয়াউর রহমান**; Khaled Mosharraf was killed. (Parties describe this day differently.)

## Ziaur Rahman (1975–1981)
- Became **President on 21 April 1977**; confirmed by a **referendum (30 May 1977)**.
- 🔥 **First presidential election by direct vote: 3 June 1978** — Zia defeated **General M. A. G. Osmani**.
- Founded the **Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP)** on **1 September 1978**.
- **Second parliamentary election: 18 February 1979** (BNP won a majority). The **5th amendment (1979)** ratified the martial-law period.
- Zia was **assassinated on 30 May 1981** at the **Chattogram Circuit House**. Vice-President **Justice আবদুস সাত্তার** became acting President and then won the presidential election (November 1981).

## H. M. Ershad (1982–1990)
- 🔥 **24 March 1982:** Army chief **হুসেইন মুহম্মদ এরশাদ** seized power in a bloodless coup and declared **martial law**.
- Founded the **Jatiya Party** (1 January 1986). Parliamentary elections: **3rd — 7 May 1986**, **4th — 3 March 1988** (boycotted by the main opposition).
- **8th amendment (1988):** Islam made the state religion.
- Anti-Ershad movement: **নূর হোসেন** was killed on **10 November 1987** with "স্বৈরাচার নিপাত যাক, গণতন্ত্র মুক্তি পাক" written on his body. **Dr. মিলন** was killed on 27 November 1990.
- 🔥 **6 December 1990:** Ershad **resigned** after a mass uprising. Chief Justice **সাহাবুদ্দীন আহমদ** became acting President and headed a neutral interim (caretaker) government.

## Parliamentary democracy (1991 onward)
| Parliament | Election date | Result / key fact |
|---|---|---|
| 5th | 🔥 **27 Feb 1991** | BNP; **খালেদা জিয়া** — **first woman Prime Minister** |
| — | 1991 | **12th amendment**: parliamentary system restored (referendum 15 Sep 1991) |
| 6th | **15 Feb 1996** | Boycotted by major opposition; passed the **13th amendment (caretaker government)**; shortest parliament |
| 7th | **12 June 1996** | Awami League; **শেখ হাসিনা** PM. **Ganges Water Treaty** (Dec 1996), **CHT Peace Accord** (2 Dec 1997) |
| 8th | **1 Oct 2001** | BNP-led four-party alliance; Khaleda Zia PM |
| — | **11 Jan 2007** | State of emergency ("1/11"); army-backed caretaker government under **ফখরুদ্দীন আহমদ** |
| 9th | **29 Dec 2008** | Awami League-led grand alliance; Sheikh Hasina PM. **15th amendment (2011)** abolished the caretaker system |
| 10th | **5 Jan 2014** | Boycotted by BNP-led alliance; **153** seats won unopposed |
| 11th | **30 Dec 2018** | Awami League-led alliance |
| 12th | **7 Jan 2024** | Awami League; boycotted by BNP |

## 2024 change of government 🔥
- **July–August 2024:** a student-led **quota-reform movement** grew into a mass uprising against the government; hundreds of people were killed.
- **5 August 2024:** Prime Minister **Sheikh Hasina resigned and left the country**.
- **6 August 2024:** President **মোহাম্মদ সাহাবুদ্দিন** dissolved the 12th parliament.
- **8 August 2024:** an **interim government** was sworn in, headed by **Chief Adviser ড. মুহাম্মদ ইউনূস** (Nobel Peace laureate, 2006). It set up reform commissions (constitution, election, judiciary, public administration, police, anti-corruption, etc.).

> 🔄 Update: a national election and constitutional reforms were planned after the interim period. Check the result of the latest parliamentary election and the current Prime Minister and President in a newspaper.

## Quick revision
- First parliamentary election: **7 March 1973** (AL 293/300).
- 4th amendment / one-party system: **25 January 1975**; BAKSAL **24 February 1975**.
- Bangabandhu assassinated: **15 August 1975**.
- Jail killing of four national leaders: **3 November 1975**.

- First woman PM: **Khaleda Zia (1991)**.
- Caretaker system: **13th amendment (1996)**; abolished by **15th (2011)**.
- Interim government under **Dr. Muhammad Yunus**: **8 August 2024**.

BD-16.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask the key dates (4 November / 16 December 1972), the drafting committee chairman (Dr. Kamal Hossain), the number of parts and articles, and "which article says what" for Part I and Part II (state principles).

## Making of the Constitution 🔥🔥
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 11 Jan 1972 | **Provisional Constitution Order** (অস্থায়ী সংবিধান আদেশ) — parliamentary system |
| 23 Mar 1972 | Constituent Assembly (গণপরিষদ) Order issued |
| **10 Apr 1972** | **First session of the Constituent Assembly**; Speaker **শাহ আবদুল হামিদ** |
| 11 Apr 1972 | **34-member drafting committee** formed; chairman 🔥 **ড. কামাল হোসেন** (Law Minister) |
| 12 Oct 1972 | Draft bill placed in the Constituent Assembly |
| 🔥 **4 Nov 1972** | **Constitution adopted** by the Constituent Assembly — **Constitution Day (সংবিধান দিবস)** |
| 14 Dec 1972 | Members signed the handwritten copy |
| 🔥 **16 Dec 1972** | **Constitution came into force** |

- The drafting committee's only **woman member**: **রাজিয়া বানু**. The only **opposition member**: **সুরঞ্জিত সেনগুপ্ত** (he did not sign in protest).
- The members of the Constituent Assembly were those elected in 1970 to the National and Provincial Assemblies from East Pakistan (the total is commonly given as **403**).
- The original was **handwritten** (calligraphy by **এ. কে. এম. আবদুর রউফ**); artwork by a team under **শিল্পাচার্য জয়নুল আবেদিন** (including **হাশেম খান**).
- There are **Bangla and English** texts; if they conflict, the **Bangla text prevails** (Article 153).

## Features 🔥
- **Written** and **rigid** (amendment needs a **two-thirds** majority of the total MPs — Article 142).
- **Unitary** state; **parliamentary** government (restored in 1991); **unicameral** legislature.
- **Supremacy of the Constitution** (Article 7); independent judiciary with **judicial review**.
- Structure today: **11 parts**, **153 articles**, **7 schedules** (the 5th–7th schedules were added in 2011).

| Part | Subject | Articles |
|---|---|---|
| I | The Republic | 1–7B |
| II | Fundamental Principles of State Policy | 8–25 |
| III | Fundamental Rights | 26–47A |
| IV | The Executive | 48–64 |
| V | The Legislature | 65–93 |
| VI | The Judiciary | 94–117 |
| VII | Elections | 118–126 |
| VIII | Comptroller and Auditor-General | 127–132 |
| IX | Services of Bangladesh | 133–141 |
| IXA | Emergency Provisions | 141A–141C |
| X | Amendment of the Constitution | 142 |
| XI | Miscellaneous | 143–153 |

## Part I — The Republic 🔥
| Article | Subject |
|---|---|
| **1** | Bangladesh is a **unitary, independent, sovereign Republic** — **"গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ"** |
| **2** | Territory of the Republic |
| **2A** | **State religion: Islam**; other religions have equal status and equal rights |
| 🔥 **3** | **State language: Bangla** |
| **4** | **National anthem, flag and emblem** (anthem: first **10 lines** of "আমার সোনার বাংলা") |
| **4A** | Portrait of the Father of the Nation (added 2011) |

## Key details asked 🔥
### Article 33 — arrest and detention
- An arrested person must be **told the grounds** of arrest and has the right to **consult and be defended by a lawyer** of his choice.
- 🔥 He must be produced before the **nearest magistrate within 24 hours** (excluding travel time), and cannot be kept longer without the magistrate's order.
- These safeguards do not apply to an **enemy alien** or a person held under **preventive detention**. Preventive detention beyond **six months** needs the report of an **Advisory Board**.

### Article 35 — trial and punishment
- No **ex post facto** punishment (no punishment under a law made after the act).
- No **double jeopardy** (not tried or punished twice for the same offence).
- Right to a **speedy and public trial** by an independent court.
- No person can be **compelled to be a witness against himself**.
- No **torture** or cruel, inhuman or degrading punishment.

### Article 39 — speech and press
- Freedom of thought and conscience is **guaranteed** (absolute).
- Freedom of speech and of the press is subject to **reasonable restrictions** by law: state security, friendly relations with foreign states, public order, decency or morality, contempt of court, defamation, incitement to an offence.

### Citizens only vs. all persons
- Most rights are for **citizens** (e.g. Art. 27, 36–40).
- Some protect **every person** in Bangladesh, including foreigners: e.g. **Art. 32** (life and liberty), **33** (arrest), **34** (forced labour), **35** (trial).

| **Prohibition** (নিষেধাজ্ঞা) | Stops a lower court/tribunal from exceeding jurisdiction |

| **Quo warranto** (কারণ দর্শাও) | "By what authority?" — challenges an unlawful holder of public office |

## Rights during an emergency
- When an emergency is proclaimed (**Article 141A**):
  - 🔥 **Article 141B:** the freedoms in **Articles 36–40 and 42** are suspended for the emergency period.
  - **Article 141C:** the President may suspend the **right to move any court** to enforce the fundamental rights named in his order.

## How the Constitution is amended 🔥
- **Article 142** (Part X): a bill to amend must be passed by at least **two-thirds of the total members** of Parliament.
- The President must assent within **7 days**; otherwise it is deemed assented.
- **Article 7B** (added 2011): the preamble, Parts I and II, most of Part III, and some other basic provisions **cannot be amended**.

## The Prime Minister (প্রধানমন্ত্রী) 🔥

- 🔥 The President appoints as PM the MP who **appears to command the support of the majority** of MPs (Art. 56(3)).
- The PM's office falls vacant if he/she resigns, ceases to be an MP, or loses majority support (Art. 57).
- Leader of the House in Parliament.

## The Cabinet (মন্ত্রিসভা) 🔥
- Headed by the PM; **collectively responsible to Parliament** (Art. 55).
- Ranks: **Minister**, **State Minister (প্রতিমন্ত্রী)**, **Deputy Minister (উপমন্ত্রী)**.
- 🔥 At least **nine-tenths** of ministers must be MPs; up to **one-tenth** may be non-MPs ("technocrat ministers") (Art. 56(2)).
- Government business is run under the **Rules of Business** (1996) and the **Allocation of Business**.
- **Cabinet Division**, headed by the **Cabinet Secretary** — the senior-most civil servant. The **Bangladesh Secretariat** is in Dhaka.
- Warrant of precedence (first three): **President → Prime Minister → Speaker**.

BD-21.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask the name and size of Parliament, quorum, gap between sessions, the architect of the Sangsad Bhaban, the first and first woman Speaker, who administers which oath, and the standing committees (especially the Public Accounts Committee).

## Jatiya Sangsad (জাতীয় সংসদ) 🔥
- Article **65**: Parliament is called the **"জাতীয় সংসদ" (House of the Nation)**. It is **unicameral** (এক কক্ষ বিশিষ্ট).
- 🔥 **350 members**: **300** directly elected from single-member territorial constituencies + **50 reserved women's seats**.
- Reserved women members are **elected by the 300 MPs** in proportion to party strength (they are not directly elected by the people).
- Constituency **no. 1 is Panchagarh-1**; **no. 300 is Bandarban** (Parbatya Bandarban).
- Qualification: citizen, **25 years** old (Art. 66).
- Term: **5 years** from the first meeting (Art. 72).
- 🔥 Gap between two sessions: **not more than 60 days** (Art. 72).
- 🔥 **Quorum: 60 members** (Art. 75).
- Voter age: **18 years**.
- **Floor crossing** (Art. 70): an MP loses the seat if he resigns from his party or votes against it.

## Sangsad Bhaban (সংসদ ভবন) 🔥
- Designed by American architect 🔥 **লুই আই. কান (Louis I. Kahn)**.
- At **শেরে বাংলা নগর**, Dhaka. Work began in the early 1960s (Pakistan period); inaugurated on **28 January 1982**.
- Before that, Parliament sat in the old **Tejgaon** building (now the Prime Minister's Office).

## Speaker (স্পিকার) 🔥
- Article **74**: the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are elected by the MPs from among themselves.
- Presides over Parliament; decides whether a bill is a **money bill**; keeps order.
- 🔥 Acts as **President** when the office is vacant or the President is absent (Art. 54).
- The **President's oath** is administered by the **Speaker**.

| Fact | Answer |
|---|---|
| First Speaker (Constituent Assembly, 1972) | **শাহ আবদুল হামিদ** |
| First Speaker of the first Jatiya Sangsad (1973) | **মোহাম্মদ মোহাম্মদুল্লাহ** |
| 🔥 **First woman Speaker** (and youngest) | **ড. শিরীন শারমিন চৌধুরী** (2013) |

## Law-making 🔥
- **Ordinary bill:** introduced by a minister (government bill) or an ordinary MP (**private member's bill**); three readings; then sent to the President, who must assent within **15 days** (Art. 80).
- **Money bill** (Art. 81): can be introduced only with the **President's recommendation**; the Speaker certifies it.
- **Budget (annual financial statement, Art. 87):** presented by the **Finance Minister** usually in **June**; fiscal year **1 July – 30 June**.
- **Constitution amendment bill** (Art. 142): needs **two-thirds** of total MPs.
- Tools of control: **question hour**, adjournment motion, point of order, **walkout**, **no-confidence**, and committees.

## Parliamentary committees (সংসদীয় কমিটি) 🔥
- Article **76** provides for **standing committees**.
- 🔥 **Public Accounts Committee (PAC, সরকারি হিসাব সম্পর্কিত কমিটি)** — examines government accounts and the **CAG's audit reports**; generally regarded as the most important committee.
- **Estimates Committee** — examines budget estimates.
- **Committee on Public Undertakings** — examines state enterprises.
- **Committee on Privileges**, **Committee on Government Assurances**, **Petition Committee**, **Library Committee**, **House Committee**.
- **Business Advisory Committee** and **Rules of Procedure Committee** — chaired by the **Speaker**.
- **Standing committees on ministries** — one for each ministry. Since the 7th Parliament (1996–2001) they have been chaired by **MPs, not ministers**.
